description:
About the Position

This doctorate develops mathematical approaches for transport and logistics decisions involving multiple organisations. It considers how competition and cooperation change the choices available to each participant.

Research Position Overview

Combine game theory with mixed-integer optimisation. Develop scalable algorithms using methods such as column generation, branch-and-price and Benders decomposition.

Research Areas

  • Operations research
  • Game theory
  • Large-scale mathematical optimisation

Funding and Duration

Employment and financial support
ComponentDetails
PositionPaid doctoral employee
Salary€3,204–€4,051 gross/month; first-to-fourth-year progression
Additional pay8% holiday allowance; 8.3% year-end bonus
DurationFour years in principle: 18 months initially, then 30 months after satisfactory assessment
Programme / supportSalaried TU Delft doctoral employment.

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic and research preparation
CriterionRequirement
Academic preparationMSc in operations research, econometrics, applied mathematics, computer science, industrial engineering, systems/control or a related field.
Relevant skillsMixed-integer optimisation, programming and solver experience; game theory or decomposition knowledge is advantageous.
EnglishRequired; see TU Delft’s admission policy for accepted evidence and exemptions.
Specific conditionsThe advert contains inconsistent hours/FTE fields; confirm the working-hours arrangement with the recruiter.

Application dates

Recruitment information
ComponentDetails
StatusOpen when verified against the official source
Deadline22 November 2026
Start dateNot specified
LocationDelft, Netherlands

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 22 November 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

  • CV and motivation letter addressed to Patrick Stokkink.

Use the application button on the official advert; email enquiries do not replace an online application.

About TU Delft and the Host Faculty

TU Delft is a technical university in Delft, Netherlands. This position is hosted by the Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management. Doctoral employment includes Graduate School training and supervision.

No IELTS or TOEFL certificate is requested for this employed Dutch position; English is assessed through the application documents and an interview in English.
